_README: Same car and same PARTS as gearing-gr86-2026-08-12.json, with the TUNE
reset to the game's default. Boston restored the default tune while keeping
the upgrades, which is the control row group C1 is built around and is
better than anything the plan asked for: the app's tune and the game's
default, on one build, nothing else moved.
It was taken to measure the panel's repeat variance. It did that, and then
produced two findings that matter far more — see repeatTest, spreadDefect
screen: tuning menu — GEARING tab, game default tune restored

build.buildNote: IDENTICAL to the sibling fixture. Only the tune changed.

held.ratiosNote: The GAME'S OWN default ratios for this car with a race transmission fitted. See spreadDefect — these are not SPREAD[7].

varied: nothing — the same setting re-entered six times

readings.axisNote: 159, on the SAME PARTS that read 157 with the app's tune applied. See axisMovedWithTune.

repeatTest: THE RESULT: the panel is effectively deterministic, and the claim this
test was run to overturn was substantially right after all.
Six reads of one setting, three approached by moving the slider up and
back, three by moving it down and back:
0-60        3.350  x6   identical
0-100       8.717  x6   identical
top speed   141.1  x6   identical
60-0         63.1  x6   identical
lateral G   1.25 / 1.41 x6   identical
MB / AB / aero eff  0.50 / 0.45 / 0.750  x6   identical
No difference between the from-above and from-below groups, so there is no
path dependence in how a slider is approached — which was the worse of the
two things this test could have found.
THE CORRECTION THIS FORCES ON THE PREVIOUS COMMIT. Boston reported that
moving off a value and back moves the figures slightly, and CLAUDE.md and
BACKLOG.md were edited to say the panel is not noise-free. Measured, that
was too strong: the resolution of the effect is 0.1 ft on the longest
figure on the screen, once in six. Both files are corrected back, with the
measurement rather than either assertion.
AND WHAT THAT COSTS THE SIBLING FIXTURE. Top speed there went 139.9, 139.9,
139.5, 139.7 across final drives 0.04 apart, and that was written up as the
readout resampling itself. It is not. With repeat variance at zero, that
non-monotonicity is a REAL property of the gearing, and the sibling file is
corrected to say so. A 0.4 mph difference on this panel is a result.
spreadDefect: THE BIG ONE. The game's default ratios for this car with a race box are
and SPREAD[7] in index.html:531 is
They are not close, and every gear is wider apart than the app assumes.
WHERE THE OLD 'CONFIRMATION' CAME FROM. CLAUDE.md lists the SPREAD tables
as tier 1, confirmed on Boston's screen 2026-07-31, on the strength of a
screen showing exactly 2.92/2.05/1.60/1.30/1.10/0.95/0.82. The sibling
fixture repeated that claim this morning. Both were reading the app's OWN
ratio set back off a car it had been applied to. That is circular, and it
is the tidiest possible example of the failure this repo keeps writing
warnings about: the wrong version was more confident, because the numbers
matched exactly.
WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic. index.html:1083 takes the top ratio
straight from SPREAD to build the speed constant:
topGear = SPREAD[gr][gr-1]        -> 0.82 assumed, 0.85 actual
kSpeed  = vgraph * fdfit * topGear
so on a car running the game's ratios, k is out by 0.82/0.85 = 3.5%, and
index.html:1146 then computes every per-gear speed from the same wrong
table. The gear speeds the card prints are for a gearbox the car does not
have.
THE ONE THING THAT RESCUES IT: the app also EMITS a ratio set (ratioSet(),
index.html:879), and if the user applies it then SPREAD is what is on the
car and everything is self-consistent. That is exactly the state the
sibling fixture was measured in, which is why its k = 588.3 is still
correct FOR THAT SETUP. So this is not 'the gearing maths is wrong', it is
'the app assumes its own ratios are fitted and never says so'.
WHAT IT MEANS FOR CASE G4. G4 exists to transcribe the default ratios for
4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 gears because those rows 'look interpolated off a
curve'. They are worse than interpolated — the ONE row believed to be
measured is now the one known to be wrong. G4 is promoted to the top of
the queue, and its first row is a 7-speed, which was supposedly done.
axisMovedWithTune: The axis read 157 on this car with the app's tune, and reads 159 with the
game's default tune. THE PARTS DID NOT CHANGE. Boston's standing
observation was that only changing parts moves it; this shows the tune
moves it too.
That is very likely the whole of E2. July recorded 157 and 159 for the same
car and nobody could see how both could be real. Two tunes on one build is
how: neither reading was a mistake, and the defect was never recording
which tune was loaded.
IT IS NOT ATTRIBUTED YET, and must not be written up as if it were.
Restoring the default tune moved everything at once — ratios, final drive,
aero, springs, the lot. Three candidates, in order of how plausible they
are:
1. THE TOP RATIO. 0.82 -> 0.85. If the axis is drawn from what the top
gear can reach, this is the direct mechanism.
2. AERO. Aero Efficiency moved 0.741 -> 0.750 and measured top speed
moved 139.9 -> 141.1, both in the same direction as the axis. If the
axis tracks the car's drag-limited capability, this is it.
3. Something else in the tune entirely.
THE EXPERIMENT THAT SEPARATES THEM, two readings from the default tune:
change ONLY the 7th gear ratio and re-read the axis; put it back, change
ONLY the rear wing and re-read. One variable each, five minutes, and it
closes E2 properly instead of by argument.
Note this does NOT overturn G2. The axis held at 157 across final drives
3.50 to 4.60 with the ratios fixed, so it is still not a function of the
final drive.
notes: The default tune's own gearing is worth recording as an answer in itself: the game ships this car at final drive 3.63 with ratios spanning 4.17 to 0.85. The app's recommendation for the same car was 4.57 with a 2.92-0.82 set — shorter final drive, much narrower spread. Whether that is better is exactly what case C1 measures, and both tunes now exist on one build to measure it with. The default tune also posts better numbers on four of six panel figures than the app's tune did (0-100 8.717 vs 9.000, top speed 141.1 vs 139.9, 60-0 63.1 vs 67.1, 100-0 145.8 vs 151.8), with 0-60 slightly worse (3.350 vs 3.333) — but the two tunes differ in aero and everything else as well as gearing, so this is a flag for C1, NOT a finding.
